cohort_rule: All 40 consecutive administrative IDs 700120..700159, FIXED BEFORE opening any of them. No selection by signature count or success. Keep 404/rejected/missing; target of inference restricted to publicly retrievable records in this fixed ID band, not all petitions.
prior_exposure: Past PETITIONS5 includes petition 700143 (one of 40), but no others examined individually in this block. 700143 MUST be marked pre-exposed and excluded in sensitivity.
scope: Empirical UK citizen petition administrative participation, independent of prior UK650 election and last PETITIONS5 top-ranked design
report_asof: 2026-10-28, but source web cache may be older; do not infer current-real-time availability or first_public_at
A: Do time-stamp and data-version integrity checks reveal incorrect retrospective 'as-of' claims in independent ID-based sample, and can simple state/threshold baseline outperform signature magnitude for observed response status?

B.H1: Threshold+state baseline performs at least as well as continuous log signatures in leave-one-ID-out classification, where both classes observed
B.Hother: Strong deterministic threshold and missingness make evaluation uninformative

C: Audit opened<=threshold<=response, initial creation<=opening, updated timestamps vs closure; inspect published vs technical response date and negative lags. If n≥12 and response binary has both classes (≥3 each), implement LOOCV Brier: constant training response rate, simple indicator threshold>=10k + state, and shrinkage logistic log1p signatures. All features are realized totals, thus retrospective descriptive NOT future prediction. No model forecasts actors/elections.
R1: Unit petition-level response availability, not political success
R4: Reject leaked response date as pre-response predictor
R5: If sparse, document methodological invalidity and don't invent comparison
J: Reject pseudo-confirmation from after-event or missing data; R5 governs next action.
